decision: NOT READY FOR FULL PUBLICATION SIGN-OFF: shared analytics consent remains unresolved. Guide SEO/content checks pass.

issues.pages: All guides and other public pages using views/layout.ejs
issues.evidence: views/layout.ejs:61–68 loads gtag.js and immediately calls gtag(config). Fresh rendered dataLayer contains js/config commands, with no consent default/update; no consent UI/integration exists in the inspected tree. public/js/guide-enhancements.js itself suppresses custom events until an unambiguous grant.
issues.impact: Cannot confirm that analytics as a whole follows an explicit consent choice. The guide event gate alone is not a site-wide consent implementation.
issues.status: OPEN — pre-existing shared implementation, not introduced by the redesign; no shared tracking change authorised or applied in this review.
issues.action: Approve a focused shared-consent correction or supply/verify an existing consent integration before publication sign-off. Do not add a new tracking service. Recheck denied, granted and revoked states against actual network behaviour.

issues.evidence: The existing FAQ question and answer referred to “£100 starting payment” even when campaign.showPrice was false. Earlier checks examined only the offer card.
issues.impact: Unconfirmed/custom fallback pages could still assert an unconfirmed service price.
issues.status: FIXED — SSR price gate plus open-tab expiry removal; approved confirmed-state wording unchanged. Existing campaign regression test extended.
issues.action: 70 state cases passed, including six live expiry transitions; reduced-motion and no-JS checks cover the affected FAQ. No price, payment term or educational wording changed.

issues.evidence: Current Handbook Note 12 and FCA overview differ at exactly £5m; first-period Note 12(g)/(h) overlap. Exact approved caveat is recorded below.
issues.impact: Affected firms need their own schedule confirmed; the guide cannot resolve the regulator’s inconsistent source wording.
issues.status: OPEN EXTERNAL AMBIGUITY — appropriately qualified, not a confirmed remaining guide error.
issues.action: Keep the caveat and obtain FCA/qualified confirmation for affected firms. No substantive replacement proposed or applied.

issues.pages: Six FCA guide offers; referenced pricing page
issues.evidence: Approved config confirms £100 first month, then £100/month, six months/£600 minimum before applicable referral adjustments, separate FCA fee. vatStatement/vatShort and cancellationNotice remain null.
issues.impact: Those commercial details must be settled in the engagement process; the audit cannot invent them.
issues.status: UNCHANGED — current approved terms and conditional handling preserved.
issues.action: Business confirmation of missing VAT/cancellation details is separate commercial work. No values or promises added.

issues.severity: Important, non-blocking to this guide change
issues.evidence: Pricing has an existing unguarded paragraph beginning “Following FCA authorisation, the existing £100 monthly subscription continues…”. The service page retains “FCA applications can take 6–12 months.” with completeness/complexity and no-guarantee qualifications. Guides omit that promotional timing line.
issues.impact: The pricing paragraph remains price-bearing under a future unconfirmed fallback; the service timing headline is less precise than the corrected guide. Neither contradicts the current confirmed guide price.
issues.status: OPEN — existing non-guide content preserved; not silently changed.
issues.action: Seek separate approval for the non-guide fallback correction and, optionally, more precise service-page timing wording. Current campaign fallback is confirmed continuation.

issues.evidence: Local API returns 503 by design. Fresh GET-only check of the existing live booking flow returned availability 200 and reached the details step. The local deployment .env copy lacks BOOKING_API_KEY and CUSTOMER_ID_FLOOR; actual Render secrets/settings were not accessible.
issues.impact: The local .env copy is not proof of the Render environment. Production startup requires the existing persistent database, a reconciled CUSTOMER_ID_FLOOR and valid session configuration. No completed booking or notification test was performed.
issues.status: PARTIALLY VERIFIED — current live read-only flow works; actual host settings and final deployed build remain unverified.
issues.action: Verify host configuration before release; retain the existing real values. Do not guess a customer ID floor or copy local DB/secrets to production. Never count a click or details screen as a booking completion.

issues.evidence: Supplied pre-publication page table: licence 232/0/4.90; eligibility 234/2/7.07; limited permission 67/0/8.03; credit broking 38/0/6.13 (impressions/clicks/average position).
issues.impact: These pages merit post-publication snippet and query/page review, but the data does not establish which query belongs to which page or prove cannibalisation.
issues.action: Collect query-by-page/device data over a comparable post-publication period; consider targeted changes only if supported. Do not infer gains from unpublished changes.

issues.severity: Optional future work requiring editorial approval
issues.pages: Credit broking; website compliance; hub; Article markup
issues.evidence: AR/IAR in the credit-broking guide and CONC/APR in the website guide could be defined at first use. Genuine authorship/reviewer information and representative article imagery are not available in the approved content. Hub uses Article with real editorial content.
issues.impact: Potential clarity and semantic improvements, not indexing blockers.
issues.action: Propose short first-use definitions for approval. Add real author/reviewer information only when confirmed. Consider CollectionPage/ItemList for the hub later; do not fabricate Article dates or images.

existing: The FCA’s consumer-credit application notes describe the legal determination period as the earlier of six months from receipt of a completed application or twelve months from receipt of an incomplete application.

The FCA’s 2026/27 Q1 metrics set a 95% target of four months for complete new Part 4A authorisation applications and ten months for incomplete applications. Part 4A is the authorisation route for permission to carry on regulated activities.
A target is not an average, an approval rate or a guaranteed decision date. Preparation before submission is separate.
sourceEvidence.classification: No confirmed factual error in the current guide
sources: Page 3, Timings for this application: earlier-of legal determination periods
Page 1, A1.1: new-firm Part 4A operating target
sourceEvidence.finding: The current table distinguishes formal six/twelve-month assessment periods from the 95% four/ten-month operating target. Neither is presented as an average, approval rate or guarantee. Preparation and the six-month commercial term remain separate. No replacement proposed.

sourceEvidence.existing: At exactly £5 million, the ongoing Handbook rule uses “£5 million or less” for annual reporting, but the FCA overview uses “£5m or more” for twice-yearly reporting. Note 12(g) and (h) also overlap at that boundary for firms entering scope in January–June from 2026. Ask the FCA to confirm the applicable schedule if this affects your firm; this guide does not resolve that official inconsistency.
sourceEvidence.classification: Official-source inconsistency, explicitly qualified in the approved text
sources: SUP 16.12.29CR Note 12(c)–(i), freshly rendered in Chromium
When to report; Check your schedule
sourceEvidence.finding: Ongoing Handbook rules separate at/below £5m from above £5m and specify January–June plus January–December for larger firms. The FCA overview includes the exact boundary in the larger group; first-period paragraphs (g)/(h) also overlap there. The guide says to seek FCA confirmation for affected firms. Retain this qualification; do not silently pick an interpretation.

sources: Owned/non-owned stock, part-exchange and sourcing scenario tables
sourceEvidence.finding: The approved guide retains the conditional nature of the examples and distinguishes lending, sourcing and introductions. No definitive permission assessment or approval claim added.

sourceEvidence.classification: Valid local markup checks; enhancement eligibility is separate
sources: Recommended properties; no required Article properties

Publisher and page entity references resolve to the site graph. Missing verified author, publication date and representative Article image are not fabricated; these remain optional editorial/schema work. No Google Rich Results Test certification claimed.
